details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: TOCTOU symlink traversal in getfacl, setfacl and chacl
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-54370.patch: walk trees through directory file
       descriptors and act on the final pathname component with symlink-safe
       calls in tools/getfacl.c, tools/setfacl.c, tools/do_set.c and
       tools/chacl.c
     - the *at() ACL operations the hardened tools need are private helpers in
       tools/acl_at.c, so libacl's public ABI and installed headers are
       unchanged
     - setfacl --restore is symlink-safe only when invoked with -P: without it
       the backup's pathnames are still resolved by name, so stat, chown,
       chmod and the ACL write still follow symlinks; upstream's warning about
       that is built out with --disable-unsafe-restore-warnings, so --restore
       output is unchanged for scripts that parse stderr
     - getfacl -P and setfacl -P now fail with ELOOP on a symlink argument
       instead of silently ignoring it
     - in the recursive default mode a toplevel symlink-to-directory argument
       is now descended into, where 2.2.53 applied to the toplevel entry only;
       'setfacl -R <symlink-to-dir>' therefore writes to the whole subtree
       (upstream 2.4.0 walk_tree semantics)
     - chacl on a symlink given on the command line now fails with "Operation
       not supported" instead of acting on the symlink's target
     - getfacl no longer strips a leading './' from pathnames, so
       'getfacl -R ./dir' prints '# file: ./dir' for the toplevel entry
     - the symlink-safe paths need /proc mounted: without it getfacl and
       setfacl warn and then fail with EACCES ("Permission denied"), instead
       of falling back to the ACL derived from the file mode, which would
       drop every named entry and still exit successfully
     - debian/rules: configure with --disable-unsafe-restore-warnings, and
       skip test/root/permissions.test and test/root/setfacl.test on build
       hosts whose build tree is not reachable by unprivileged users, where
       they fail regardless of this patch
     - CVE-2026-54370
